buckets.title: Landing page components
buckets.description: Structural building blocks you rearrange to keep a single CTA honest.

terms.title: Hero
terms.shortDescription: The above-the-fold stage that introduces the offer and CTA immediately.
terms.definition: The hero pairs a clear headline, a proof-backed supporting line, and the primary CTA so visitors know what you do and what to do next without scrolling.
terms.whenToUse: Always—the hero is the first impression for any paid or organic visit.
aiPhrases: Draft a hero layout that locks headline, supporting copy, and CTA in a tight Z-pattern.
examples: Headline + subhead on the left, product mock and primary CTA on the right.

terms.title: Subhead
terms.shortDescription: One tight sentence that clarifies value right after the hero headline.
terms.definition: The subhead answers the immediate follow-up question the headline triggers—usually who it is for or what result they get next.
terms.whenToUse: Whenever the headline is bold or outcome-focused and needs context to feel believable.
aiPhrases: Write a subhead that names the audience and promises the outcome in under 18 words.
examples: Designed for growth teams shipping tests weekly

terms.title: Primary CTA
terms.shortDescription: The one action button styled for maximum contrast and clarity.
terms.definition: Your primary CTA uses an action verb, a benefit hint, and surrounding reassurance to make the click feel obvious.
terms.whenToUse: Always present in the hero and repeated within the flow where intent peaks.
aiPhrases: Give me three CTA variants that pair an active verb with the next-step benefit.

terms.title: Value props
terms.shortDescription: Three to five punchy proof-backed statements that ladder up to the promise.
terms.definition: Value props are scannable headlines with a short line of support that show how you deliver the main outcome.
terms.whenToUse: Use when visitors need to understand how the product/system works in their context.
aiPhrases: Summarize the top four outcomes as value props with proof metrics or specific details.
examples: Cut build time from weeks to hours with a subline about modular sections

terms.title: Features
terms.shortDescription: Deeper dives that show the mechanics behind each value prop.
terms.definition: Feature blocks combine visuals, captions, and specifics so buyers trust that the promised outcome is doable.
terms.whenToUse: After value props to let detail-oriented readers continue their evaluation.
aiPhrases: Outline three feature cards with titles, supporting copy, and an optional screenshot cue.
examples: Component library, Test dashboard, Collaboration timeline

terms.title: Social proof bar
terms.shortDescription: Logos, usage stats, or quick trust badges that calm hesitation.
terms.definition: A slim strip or cluster that shows recognizable customers, outcomes, or expert quotes without hijacking the main CTA.
terms.whenToUse: Drop near the hero or right before the primary CTA repeats.
aiPhrases: Write a social proof bar headline plus three credibility stats tied to the landing page offer.
examples: Trusted by 1,200+ GTM teams • 3.8M experiments shipped

terms.title: Testimonials
terms.shortDescription: Longer-form customer quotes paired with names, roles, and outcomes.
terms.definition: Testimonials translate proof into narrative—showing what changed, how fast, and what metric moved.
terms.whenToUse: After value props or near pricing to reinforce belief before commitment.
aiPhrases: Turn this case study into a two-sentence testimonial with a named role and quant result.
examples: “We doubled signups in 45 days once we enforced the attention ratio rules.”

terms.title: FAQ
terms.shortDescription: Answer the top objections before someone bounces to support.
terms.definition: The FAQ clusters 4-6 questions ordered by frequency so teams feel confident clicking the CTA.
terms.whenToUse: Near the bottom or beside pricing when adoption blockers surface.
aiPhrases: List the top five questions a skeptical buyer asks before trying this landing page system.
examples: “How long does setup take?” with a 90-minute reassurance

terms.title: Pricing table
terms.shortDescription: Side-by-side comparison of plans or the single offer summary.
terms.definition: Pricing tables outline cost, inclusions, and commitment so there’s no mystery before the CTA.
terms.whenToUse: Whenever the landing page is selling a specific plan, package, or service tier.
aiPhrases: Compose a single-offer pricing module with price, inclusions, and a risk reducer.
examples: Growth Plan – $2,400/mo • includes CRO lead, playbook, and build crew

terms.title: Footer CTA
terms.shortDescription: Final call-to-action for visitors who read everything.
terms.definition: A mirrored primary CTA paired with contact details or a low-friction alternate action for fence sitters.
terms.whenToUse: Always repeat the CTA at the bottom for high-intent scrollers.
aiPhrases: Write a footer CTA block with a headline, CTA button, and trust microcopy.
examples: Ready to ship cleaner pages? → Book the 20-minute teardown
